protocol.primary_metric: server process CPU milliseconds per semantically successful request
protocol.variation_rule: median paired CPU reduction must exceed both 8 percent and the observed baseline CPU/request relative range; otherwise inconclusive, collect more evidence
protocol.scope: Synthetic loopback read-only feed; provisional experimental budgets, no product SLO or capacity guarantee
protocol.screen: 3 alternating pairs, 2 seconds each, 0.5 second warmup, 2 workers, aggregate pacing ceiling 40 requests/s, 12000 rows, limit 1000, seed 17
protocol.mode2_confirmation: 300 second target hold per version, same configuration; 0/16/12000/100000 rows and tied-score skew screening
protocol.mode3_if_justified: Brief before implementation; 5 pairs per light/target/near-saturation regime and relevant sizes/skew; 300 second hold per version; at least 900 second finalist soak; integration, faults, resource and recovery checks
protocol.rollback: Choose preceding retained implementation and regenerate its disposable database; originals remain separate modules

load_model: Closed-loop, one outstanding request per worker; optional pacing ceiling, no catch-up. Same concurrency/pacing policy, not equal open-loop arrivals or a capacity guarantee.
reset: New deterministic DB and new server per trial; warmup excluded; OS page cache not flushed.
connection_reuse: One HTTP/1.1 connection per worker per phase; reconnect after errors; no retries.
timing: samples=[start_offset_us, elapsed_us, outcome]; 200 means matching body checksum. Nearest-rank percentiles over successful requests only, errors retained separately. Throughput uses admission plus drain elapsed. Latencies include full body read/hash.
limitations: Generator and server share host resources; CPU quota isolation unavailable.
RSS is process lifetime high water, not kernel/socket/page cache or a memory leak test.
Warmup and measured samples retained, but only measured samples enter summaries.
Expected body comes from baseline; independent contract tests must also pass.
